prerequisites: Knowledge of fundamental aspects of Electronics and Electrical Circuits
Ability to work with complex numbers, solve simple electrical circuits, and understand the basics of stochastic processes

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire fundamental notions of information transmission, signal theory, and telecommunications networks.
Design simple numerical links and simple telecommunications networks.
Understand and analyze simple telecommunication systems.
Develop effective and concise presentation skills for results.
Acquire methodological tools for the study and design of telecommunication systems useful for further studies.

syllabus_topics: Analysis of continuous-time, continuous-value, and discrete-value deterministic functions
Fourier transform of a time series
Sampling theorem in time and frequency domains and its applications
Application of signal analysis to the study of linear systems
Impulse response of a linear network
Discrete-time, continuous-value, and discrete-value random processes
Power spectrum of random PAM signals
Signals of greatest interest in telecommunications
Analog low-pass signals and related services
Numerical low-pass signals and related services
Study of an optical fiber link
Amplitude and/or angle modulated sinusoidal oscillations: AM, SSB, VSB, FM, PM, QAM
Main numerical modulations: ASK, OOK, PSK, CPFSK, M-QAM
Vector diagram and constellation of states
Switching techniques: circuit and packet switching
Layered communication architectures: ISO/OSI model and TCP/IP stack
Channel access techniques for shared communication channels: deterministic, random
Aloha solution and CSMA access strategies
IEEE 802 Project: LAN Ethernet/IEEE 802.3, Fast Ethernet/802.3u, Token Ring
teaching_methods: Examples of system and network design

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (numerical exercises, open theoretical questions, closed questions)

assessment_rules: The exam consists of only written tests with numerical exercises, open theoretical questions, and closed questions. The duration of the in-person written test is usually two hours. Grades range from 'Insufficient' (<18/30) to 'Excellent' (28-30/30 cum laude).
bibliography: L.Calandrino, G.Immovilli: "Schemi delle lezioni di Comunicazioni Elettriche" - Pitagora Editrice.
Lecture notes provided by the instructor.
institution: Università degli Studi di Modena e Reggio Emilia — Ingegneria Informatica (MO)
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Informatica (Mo) (Computer Engineering (D.M.270/04)), classe L-8 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria dell'informazione
